text_boxes.text: From transactions to evidence: what survives a change in time?
Team FraudML  |  Study: 21 November 2026  |  Workflow edition  |  Retrospective analysis

At the same review capacity, which changes improve fraud ranking -
and does the improvement persist across evaluation periods?
Follow the experiment: one controlled pipeline, two model families

3 training snapshots
F1 / F2 / valid. / test
No random-row CV

Impute, encode, scale
Clip numeric fields
Strict-past histories

Top-K hits, precision, recall
AP + paired date-block intervals
Inspect failure and date sensitivity
F1: train 223,738 / evaluate 85,610 (28 days). F2: 309,348 / 91,732 (28 days). Evaluation windows [61,89) and [89,117).
Later validation/test use one 413,378-row training snapshot; each evaluates 88,581 rows (33/31 day buckets). Expanding training sets overlap.
History uses only inputs at times <t, never labels; tied timestamps update together. Labels are assumed available at cutoff. Previously viewed test is retrospective.
Same 4 fields; missing entities keep history missing.

7 models x 3 snapshots = 21 core fits; all 9 LR fits converged. LR: balanced classes, L-BFGS, max_iter=1000; rank by margin. LightGBM [2]: 300 trees, learning rate 0.05, 31 leaves, min_child_samples=20, seed 42.

Exclude ID, target and split time from model inputs. Fit clipping, encoding, imputation and scaling on train only. Clip amount, dist1/2 and C/D/V fields; normalize entity codes. H3 uses [t-86400,t); tied-time groups update after all histories are computed.
Test: 3,083 fraud labels / 88,581 rows. The same 0.5% capacity gives 443 reviews.
Across F1/F2/validation/test, clipping (LR1-LR0) adds +27/+13/+13/+376 hits. Stronger L2 (LR2-LR1) adds -3/-1/-4/+7; no consistent extra gain.
Amount baseline: 8/443 hits; random expected hits: 15.42. LR0 probability ranking gives 6 hits, margin ranking 0: removing probability saturation alone does not fix the linear ranking.
Fraud hits at 0.5% period capacity. Budgets vary with row count; compare candidates within each period.
Y: precision (%); X: review rate. LR0 fails most at tight capacity; H0/H3 are close. Daily 8/16/32 and legacy Top100/500 are also reported.

H3-H0: change in fraud hits
1,000 paired 3-day moving-block draws; percentile 95% intervals. Four evaluation periods share the fixed protocol.
Effects change sign: +2, -11, +4, -7. All main intervals cross zero; this does not prove equivalence. More features give no stable gain; no test-based deployment winner is selected.
K = ceil(rate x N); precision = hits/K; recall = hits/fraud labels. AP = average precision, not trapezoidal PR area.
V323 daily median, nonmissing values; orange band marks days 171-172.

49 to 1,411: V323 train/test maximum.
442 of LR0's top 443 reviews come from the two dates; all 443 are false positives.

394 columns x 3 partitions: missingness, quantiles, constants, non-finite/unseen values and train-range exceedances. Drift, score contributions and date concentration support an extreme-input diagnosis, not a unique cause.
Duplicate audit: 1,215 input groups (ID/label/time excluded); 399 cross partitions, 17 mixed-label. No automatic deduplication.
16 reviews/day = 496 test slots; global ranking gets exactly the same total.
LR0 daily advantage: +301, 3-day 95% interval [-38, 341.02]; omitting two dates gives -8. LR2 still leads by 87 period hits (362 vs 275; 414 slots).
Test H3-H0 = -7 hits. Post-hoc block-length comparison:
All 332 continuous 1/2/7-day omissions keep scores/history/models fixed and rematch budgets. The 7-day interval is negative; 1/3-day intervals cross zero.
31 test days limit small-effect and long-term claims. Fixed-model intervals omit training uncertainty/multiplicity correction. Uncalibrated scores; no deployment, causal or financial benefit.

Supplement verification also checks 126 focused quantiles and 28 baseline groups. Three legacy reruns retain numerical/environment differences. Clean isolated installation: pip check, 10 tests and synthetic end-to-end passed; no full real-data refit in that environment. Source, code and artifact hashes are retained.
Train-only clipping repairs much of the LR failure.
History gains did not persist across periods.
Obtain a genuinely unseen labeled period next.

Retrospective study; assumed review budgets and label availability. Sources: verified study_20261121_01; executed_summary.json; supplement_20261121_01; frozen plan2. [1] Kaggle/Vesta, IEEE-CIS (2019). [2] Ke et al., LightGBM, NeurIPS (2017).
